candidates.name: armin-one-lead-support-layers
candidates.summary: One lead carries the track, dry and centered; all other layers (doubled synths, reverb tails, vocal stacks) exist only to support it. Toggle test: without support layers the track loses its soul, with them the lead pierces at its peak. Sessions run to 110 channels; a piano recording becomes a 75-layer club track; quantizing to the grid costs human feel but makes layering at scale possible.

candidates.name: irisloops-swing-bounce-hats
candidates.summary: Tech-house bounce from hat swing at 125 BPM: kick straight on every beat, hats on every sixteenth, every second sixteenth delayed (start mid-50s percent, raise to around 60 percent; video demos 55 percent then 62 percent, straight 50 percent vs swung 62 percent A/B); only hats and percussion swing; off-beat hats slightly lower in level. Evidence: creator own written breakdown on own account plus matching video demo, with independent MPC/DAW percent-convention corroboration (50 percent = straight). OPEN: whether the bass also swings is unanswered (commenter asked, reel names hats/percussion only) — do not assert it. Counterpoint carried: straight timing works sometimes too; swing is a choice for bounce, not a law.
